newsitem.title: USA: Midday CSCE coffee mixed in thin, choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: Midday CSCE coffee mixed in thin, choppy trade.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were mixed in choppy trading ahead of midday, with the spot September contract lifted by commission house buying, floor sources said.
Dealings, however, were exceedlingly thin at an estimated 1,109 lots as of 1100 EDT.
"It very quiet," said one trader. "All the locals are over at sugar and the absence of locals has hurt the market. There's no follow-through or movement."
At 1149, September arabicas were up 0.90 cent at 185.40 cents a lb, traded 187.00 to 183.25. Second-month December was 0.30 lower at 162.25, while the back months were flat to down 0.25.
Arabicas prices headed higher at the outset, defying the 1.00-cent lower pre-opening call, on light commission house short-covering, dealers said.
They said trade selling, however, kept a lid on the market.
Some dealers said forecasts calling for a slim chance of a freeze in top-grower Brazil underpinned prices.

Weather forecaster Cropcast said Friday long-range guidance models showed the greatest threat of cold weather reaching Brazil's coffee belt will be toward the middle of next week, with the probability of a freeze set at 20 percent.

However, forecaster Weather Services Corp said in its daily update today that while somewhat cooler temperatures could reach Brazil's coffee belt during the second half of the week, a high pressure expected to build in Argentina next week is likely to pass well to the south of coffee growing areas.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 190.00 cents, while support was seen at 181.00 cents.
